title: builtins.bats's @builtin-implemented arm has checked nothing since 2026-08-06: it reads the catalogue one column short, so no row ever matches
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 by vc, reading lib/builtins for 0132, and DRIVEN.

WHAT HAPPENS. The arm "every @builtin row in the catalogue has something implementing it" (tests/unit/builtins.bats) reads each catalogue row as `name lang grammar suffix rest` and takes the command line as `rest` up to ` | `. The catalogue gained a fifth column, `group`, at 9b8a5e7 (WP-07, 2026-08-06), the day after the arm was written at cc90f49. Since then `rest` starts with the group, so the command line reads as eg `Surfaces  @builtin` and never equals `@builtin`: the loop skips every row, and the arm cannot fail. The table has 27 @builtin rows; the arm has checked none of them for seven weeks.

DRIVEN at 2b9d1a5's tree: with two rows planted in lib/builtins -- a command row `zzzplant any - - Devbin @builtin` and an option row `check.zzzplant any generic ZZZPLANT - @builtin`, neither with anything behind it -- the arm is green, 1..1, ok 1. Each plant is exactly the packaging error the arm's own comment says it exists to catch.

THE ONLY OTHER POSITIONAL READER, surfaces.bats's "a catalogue row is a gate or it is not", reads grammar and suffix, the third and fourth fields, which did not move. It is sound.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO.
- Read the row with the group column, so a @builtin row is seen.
- Hold the arm's own denominator: count the rows it checked and compare that with a count taken a second way (every row whose command line is the literal @builtin), so the arm fails when it checks nothing. That is the only guard against the next column.
- Red first with the two plants, and show the fixed arm green on today's catalogue: if it is not, a packaging error has been hiding behind it.

It ships in 0.1.8 under hv's ruling. vc's (vc, 2026-09-23).

## Resolution

Fixed at a69b21b. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. The arm reads the catalogue's six fields and counts the @builtin rows it checked, against a second count taken without the column parse, so it fails when the two part company.
- RED FIRST. With a command row and an option row planted, each @builtin with nothing behind it, the old arm is green and the new one names both. The old five-field read under the new count fails "checked 0 @builtin rows, and the catalogue holds 27". On today's catalogue the fixed arm is green, 27 of 27: nothing was hiding behind it.
- REVIEW. cc reproduced the red first and approved. builtins.bats: 1..39, 39 ok.
